# PR #12754 retrospective

## Effective process

Bounded complete policy reads, fresh author eligibility, pinned object-only source and security triage preceded reviewer launches. Separate neutral assignments, supported memory controls and fresh actual-model verification preserved independent technical assessments. Both finals existed before either was read. Source inspection resolved the reported path/ownership/status questions without live browser, account, package or desktop operations. No reviewer runtime fixture was necessary; no desktop resources were claimed.

## Deviations and correction

- A coordinator combined launcher/registry discovery response exceeded the aggregate 60-line output bound. It contained owned-team metadata and launcher matches, not incomplete policy or technical evidence. Required policies had already been fully read in sequential bounded chunks. Later metadata output uses selected fields and stays bounded. Do not describe the entire process as fully compliant.
- An unsupported `herdr guide` discovery command failed without lifecycle mutation. The installed help and full `herdr --skill` text were read, and managed context plus owned Team 3 identity were verified before any lifecycle command. Preserve the failed discovery receipts.
- A guessed pair of role-prompt filenames failed an existence assertion before any reviewer dispatch. Both actual assignments were regenerated with the validated absolute `prompts/reviewer.md` path. No reviewer received a nonexistent prompt path.
- Sol recorded two exploratory source-navigation pipelines that ended with status 141 after bounded consumers stopped. They were not treated as exhaustive scans. Full patch paging and separately inspected pinned blobs support all retained claims. Native history is preserved; no invalid fixture totals exist.
- The coordinator's early broad pane-list receipt contains workspace topology returned by the CLI. Only Team 3 fields were examined for ownership and no other team's agents or resources were controlled. Prefer targeted owned-pane metadata where available.

These are process-only limitations, not concealed technical evidence failures. No test/probe was run outside review.py because no test/probe was run at all. No host configuration, service, account, browser, audio or hardware was modified. No global process or mount discovery was used. Native memory/history was not intentionally altered.

## Carry forward

Keep first-tool output rules in the actual dispatch, not only in assignment files. Keep initial discovery to filename/selected numeric or identity fields, with an aggregate 60-line output budget. Validate one absolute shared reviewer prompt path before generating assignments. Inspect source paths before constructing substitute fixtures; omit runtime work where it adds no material confidence. Distinguish source test assertions from executed test results and exact preference-value changes from unverified UI labels. Preserve API-shape uncertainties as scope limits, not speculative public findings.

## Tool and resource assessment

No confirmed review-tool or Omadev bug was discovered. Unsupported Herdr command syntax was coordinator discovery friction, not a tool bug. No Omadev slot, isolated runtime, background service or diagnostic mutable copy was created. Technical sessions and all source/report evidence are retained historically; owned agents can return to their shells after completion without removing panes.
comment:
Source inspection found two settings-ownership issues and a discarded error status at `0dc9f9c`.

### The live theme channel is shared across users

[`vivaldi-post-update`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0dc9f9c43d53e50d1b59cb5bd6f515b03f11a64a/default/vivaldi/vivaldi-post-update#L30-L38) recreates one machine-wide `style/omarchy.json`, owned by the account running the hook with mode `0644`. Every browser window's loader reads that same file, but only its owner can refresh it.

```text
Shared installation, different user themes (source-derived):
User A runs hook: channel owned by A
User B runs hook: channel recreated, now owned by B
A switches theme: channel write skipped
A's and B's browsers: both read B's channel
```

**Impact:** On a multiuser installation, live colors cross user boundaries and the earlier user's live sync stops updating. The native writer also reads appearance values from that shared channel, potentially combining one user's palette with another's rounding, blur and opacity. Its unqualified `pgrep` additionally skips a user's profile update when another user's Vivaldi is running. This does not describe a failure on an ordinary single-user desktop.

**Suggested change:** Use a user/session-specific channel selected by the corresponding browser UI, and scope the running-browser check to the current user rather than all users.

### Palette refresh also resets unrelated force-dark preferences

The [native writer](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0dc9f9c43d53e50d1b59cb5bd6f515b03f11a64a/bin/omarchy-theme-set-vivaldi#L121-L123) unconditionally assigns `False` to two preferences outside the managed theme object:

| Existing profile value | After a stopped-browser refresh |
|---|---|
| `vivaldi.appearance.force_dark_mode_theme = true` | `false` |
| `webkit.webprefs.force_dark_mode_enabled = true` | `false` |

**Impact:** Previously enabled values are lost on a theme change or the next Vivaldi launch through Omarchy. The live loader does not make these assignments, so preservation also differs depending on whether the browser was running. The exact Vivaldi settings-panel mapping was not checked.

**Suggested change:** Preserve these preferences during palette updates. If changing them is necessary for initial setup, limit that change to initialization and document the reason.

### Vivaldi refresh failures are reported as success

[`omarchy-theme-set-browser`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/0dc9f9c43d53e50d1b59cb5bd6f515b03f11a64a/bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser#L25-L37) records the policy setter's status, invokes Vivaldi refresh without checking its result, then exits with the earlier status.

```text
Policy write succeeds -> failed=0
Vivaldi profile write fails -> refresh exits nonzero
Aggregate setter -> exits 0
```

**Impact:** A malformed or unwritable Vivaldi preferences file can leave native theming stale while the aggregate command and post-update hook report success. The live path may still work.

**Suggested change:** Accumulate the Vivaldi refresh failure in `failed`, as already done for the policy setter, without clearing an earlier failure.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source-only review of the changed files and relevant callers. No tests or browser runtime were executed. The multiuser and failure paths above are source-derived, not reproduced UI results. Vivaldi preference API behavior, package installation and actual rendering remain unvalidated.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** GPT 6 Astra Medium source inspection and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, followed by source-level checking of the reported paths.
